cards.explanation: The answer is his soul. The elder prays that Gaius will prosper and enjoy good health "…as your soul also prospers." So he's saying Gaius's soul is already prospering. Nice thing to pray over a friend, friends.

The answer is hearing that his children are walking in the truth. The elder says, "I have no greater joy than to hear that my children are walking in the truth." Nothing tops it for him. Not even a fresh tray of cookies, and I don't say that lightly.

The answer is that the brothers are strangers to Gaius. The elder says Gaius is faithful in what he does for the brothers, "…and especially since they are strangers to you." Helping people who are strangers to you takes something extra, friends. Anybody can feed a friend.

The answer is in a manner worthy of God. The elder says Gaius will do well to send them on their way "…in a manner worthy of God." The bar isn't a big show. It's the way God deserves. That's a high standard, bakers, higher than any of my cookie boxes.

The answer is True. The elder says, "Therefore we ought to support such men, so that we may be fellow workers for the truth." Supporting them puts you on the team, friends. You don't have to be the one traveling to have a hand in the work.

The answer is False. The elder says Diotrephes, "…who loves to be first, will not accept our instruction." The letter went out, and Diotrephes wasn't taking it. Some folks just want the front of the line, friends.

The word is welcome. The elder says Diotrephes "…refuses to welcome the brothers…" These were traveling brothers, and the door stayed shut. I spent years in the back of a dark junk drawer before an angel called me out, so I think that stings, friends.

The answer is that he forbids them and puts them out. The elder says Diotrephes "…forbids those who want to do so, even putting them out of the church." He didn't stop at saying no for himself, friends. He blocked the others too, and that's heavy.
The word is good. The elder says, "…do not imitate what is evil, but what is good." Then he adds, "The one who does good is of God…" Copy the good stuff, bakers. It's the best recipe going.

The answer is False. Demetrius has a good testimony from everyone and from the truth itself. Then the elder adds, "We also testify for him, and you know that our testimony is true." He adds his voice to the rest, friends.
The answer is True. The elder ends with, "Greet each of our friends there by name." By name, friends, not just a wave at the crowd. That's a warm way to close a letter.
